title: Infection-associated GN: PSGN vs PIGN/IRGN
guide: The opening TYPES table contrasts PSGN with post-infective/infection-related GN across five rows — demographics, organisms and nephritogenic strains, incubation periods, presentation with its complement profile, and prognosis. Master the strain split (1/3/4/12 vs 47/49/55/57) and the C3 percentages (90% vs 60%).

title: PSGN pathogenesis, biopsy and treatment
guide: NAPlr-plasmin activates ENaC to retain Na⁺ and water, producing hypertension and pulmonary oedema. Basic urine/RFT findings, the two biopsy indications, DPGN histopathology, phase-dependent immunofluorescence (starry sky → mesangial C3 alone) and camel-hump EM deposits, plus the sign-by-sign treatment table (amlodipine 2.5–5 mg, torsemide 5–10 mg, ECG for tall T waves).

title: PSGN antibiotics, recovery, PIGN/IRGN Rx and the nephrotic–nephritic table
sec: PSGN recovery & nephrotic vs nephritic · p777
guide: Antibiotic regimens for an active sore throat and the follow-up of serum C3 to 8 weeks; management of PIGN/IRGN (garland/rope deposits, vancomycin, dialysis, no steroids); and the classic nephrotic-versus-nephritic comparison table line by line.
